Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LEC_SILABAS_COMPLEJA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Lectura de sílabas complejas*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LEC_SILABAS_COMPLEJA.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Complex syllable reading, from age 6 to 7 (7,142 administrations in 4 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .69. If the child mistakes or delays more than 5ss, the answer is scored as error. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:--------------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:----------|----------------------------:| | 2264|Sílabas complejas II |Ítems en pantalla, lectura en voz alta | 18| 0|— |60 s |fijo |Eficiencia | 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **2264.** Desordenar = No, aunque las instrucciones dicen orden al azar. 60 s. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![2264 · Sílabas complejas II](../../figuras/plataforma/2264.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 2264"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Reading syllables, words and pseudowords aloud measures **written word recognition**: converting letters into sounds and accessing the word. It is the decoding component of the simple view of reading [@hoover1990simple] and the core of dyslexia according to the IDA definition (@sec-definicion). **What distinguishes each list.** Dual-route models separate two procedures. The **sublexical route** converts graphemes into phonemes and is the only one that works for pseudowords. The **lexical route** recognizes the whole word, and it shows in words being read faster than pseudowords (lexicality effect) and frequent words faster than rare ones. In Spanish, children use both from Grade 2 [@avdyli2014lexical; @davies2013lexical]. That is why the platform has both lists: pseudowords measure pure decoding, and the difference with words estimates how much orthographic lexicon the child has built. Length (from one to four syllables) makes serial reading visible: the more the child depends on letter-by-letter conversion, the more each added syllable costs. **In a transparent orthography, what discriminates is speed.** In Spanish, almost all children read accurately by the middle of Grade 1. Children with dyslexia are accurate but read more slowly, and their reading resembles that of younger children of the same reading level: it is delayed rather than deviant development [@davies2007spanish]. A meta-analysis of 79 European studies concludes that reading speed distinguishes readers with dyslexia in all orthographies and ages, whereas accuracy depends on age and transparency [@carioti2021depth]. In German, 70% of slow readers in Grade 1 were still slow in Year 8 [@landerl2008fluency]. That is why the score in these task sheets is **correct responses per minute**, not correct responses. **What our data show.** These are the most reliable and valid tasks on the platform: - **Reliability.** Stability between terms of ρ = .65 to .81, and 2021 α between .73 and .97. - **External validity.** They predict low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency years later with a median AUC of .72 to .77 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*). The longer lists (three- and four-syllable words) predict best. - **Delay or deviance.** Comparing pseudowords with words among children of the same reading level separates delay from deviance ([Norms by reading level](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/baremo-nivel-lector.html), *in Spanish*). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.1| 2264| 2012| 631|2018/19 | 324| 320| 0| 16| | 6.2| 2264| 2011| 188|2017/18 | 762| 0| 762| 30| | 6.2| 2264| 2012| 632|2018/19 | 323| 320| 0| 16| | 6.2| 2264| 2013| 903|2019/20 | 590| 379| 211| 31| | 6.3| 90| 2010| 160|2016/17 | 931| 257| 673| 34| | 6.3| 2264| 2011| 193|2017/18 | 680| 0| 680| 30| | 6.3| 2264| 2012| 634|2018/19 | 330| 327| 0| 16| | 6.3| 90| 2012| 634|2018/19 | 329| 326| 0| 16| | 7.1| 2264| 2011| 635|2018/19 | 571| 0| 571| 25| | 7.2| 2264| 2010| 189|2017/18 | 813| 251| 561| 31| | 7.2| 2264| 2011| 636|2018/19 | 556| 0| 556| 25| | 7.3| 2264| 2010| 190|2017/18 | 430| 166| 264| 30| | 7.3| 3925| 2011| 637|2018/19 | 503| 0| 503| 24| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness|% floor |% ceiling | |----:|----------:|---:|----------:|-----:|-----:|------:|--------:|:-------|:---------| | 2264| 6.1| 320| 2012| 16.34| 14.55| 12.39| 0.57|NA |NA | | 2264| 6.2| 699| 2012, 2013| 26.64| 17.01| 28.50| 1.99|NA |NA | | 2264| 6.3| 327| 2012| 35.19| 15.62| 37.31| -0.49|NA |NA | | 90| 6.3| 583| 2010, 2012| 31.18| 15.10| 33.37| -0.55|NA |NA | | 2264| 7.2| 251| 2010| 41.65| 12.79| 43.61| -0.75|NA |NA | | 2264| 7.3| 166| 2010| 44.91| 12.62| 45.30| -0.49|NA |NA | **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct items per minute). At those time points this task cannot be used to grade difficulty. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_SILABAS_COMPLEJA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. If the same children took them, **linear equating** is also computed, which puts the second form on the scale of the first, together with the correlation between forms (parallel-forms reliability). coding under review) | 7.3| 927| -0.112| 0.087| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.3| 924| 0.020| 0.538| |School (ICC) | 7.3| 933| 0.093| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Complex syllable reading” (codes 2264 and 90; LEEDUCA battery) assesses decoding of complex syllables. The child reads aloud the stimuli shown on the screen and the examiner records each correct response or error. It comprises 30 items. The time limit is 60 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 11 sessions, from 6 to 7 years of age. The main outcome is the efficiency (correct responses per unit of time). In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .97 (N = 334, 30 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 4 months) was ρ = .72 (median of 7 session pairs; range .63–.85). Because the task is timed, α tends to overestimate reliability; stability across administrations is the preferred estimate. Stability across time points was ρ = .55–.82. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .57–.63. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 6.2 (form 2264): the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - Floor effect in the norms at 6.1 (form 2264): at least 10% of children have the worst possible score, so P10 does not exist. At those time points the "severe" and "very severe" levels must not be assigned with this task (study M3). - The task has 2 forms; in 1 of 2 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - The persistent difficulty label uses this task: validity against it is circular. - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
